# Figures (generated by tools/figures_report.py)

All in `outputs/figures/`.

## Paper candidates

- `boss_03_cumulative_gfa.png`: Cumulative built floor area, history and projection, with the population 5th-95th band.
- `boss_04_annual_gfa.png`: Annual floor area by typology and by demand type (in scope; RV units excluded by scaling).
- `boss_05_annual_carbon.png`: Annual embodied carbon by typology and by demand type (in scope).
- `boss_10_material_flows.png`: Carbon by material, annual and cumulative; soil (land-use change) on top.
- `fig_bridge.png`: Waterfall of 2026-2050 floor area by reason for building: low (S1) / reference (S3-10) / storyline (S2).
- `fig_replacement_rate.png`: Net replacement rate: census intervals (steps), S1 / S3-10 / S2 paths, BRANZ demolition rate.
- `fig_scenarios.png`: Annual floor area by scenario with the reference MC band; cumulative floor area and carbon.
- `fig_reality_checks.png`: Projection vs the 1991-2025 range (outputs/reality_checks.md) and the 2026->2027 handover.
- `fig_validation.png`: Hindcast of cumulative dwellings from 2006/2013/2018 (consistent vacancy) and the 2026 check.
- `mc_1_fan.png`: Within-scenario Monte Carlo fan (reference), history from 1991.
- `sens_1_tornado.png`: One-at-a-time sensitivities: scenarios, mix, household size, stock, near-term rule, carbon/soil bounds.
- `boss_05_annual_carbon_pb.png`: PB variant of boss_05: annual carbon by typology and demand type with the AR and AtP boundaries.
- `fig_scenarios_pb.png`: PB variant of fig_scenarios (carbon): scenarios and reference MC band vs the boundaries; cumulative vs cumulative boundaries.
- `mc_1_fan_pb.png`: PB variant of mc_1_fan (carbon): MC fan, history on the projection soil convention, base window, boundaries.
- `pb_1_boundaries.png`: Boundaries B_AR and B_AtP 2025-2050 (log axis), population modifier, table of components.
- `pb_2_loe.png`: Annual level of exceedance by principle, S1 / S3-10 / S2 with MC 5-95% bands, log axis.
- `pb_3_headroom.png`: Intensity, floor area and carbon per dwelling that would fit each boundary vs the projection (S3-10).
- `pb_4_sensitivity.png`: Tornado of cumulative LoE 2026-2050 (S3-10): source pair, GDP measure, base window, NZ population, s_sec.

## Supplementary

- `boss_01_population.png`: Population history and projection (median, 5th-95th); the 2026 level shift from observed growth.
- `boss_02_households.png`: Households: census-benchmarked to 2018, 2019-23 scaled to the 2023 census, projection from 2023.
- `boss_06_cumulative_carbon.png`: Cumulative carbon by typology and by demand type (in scope).
- `boss_07_typology_share.png`: Typology floor-area shares, history and projection (held vs trend).
- `boss_08_demographic_drivers.png`: Household size (same history treatment as boss_02) and population vs household growth.
- `boss_09_space_diagnostics.png`: Realised vs occupied floor area per new dwelling; occupancy utilisation.
- `diag_2_household_engines.png`: Household size vs arrivals (partly mechanical between censuses); DHE/consent ratio; engines.
- `diag_3_stock_bucket.png`: Vacancy definitions, stock, and dwellings per year (history by census interval).
- `diag_3b_appendix_vacancy_definition.png`: Appendix: why empty-only vacancy (not residents away) is used.
- `diag_4_floor_area.png`: Floor area by typology and demand type (history by census interval), mix, dwelling size.
- `diag_5_carbon.png`: Carbon by typology and material (history estimated with 2025 factors); case-study intensities.
- `fig_bridge_appendix_split.png`: Appendix: the bridge with demolition and residual split (split assumes the BRANZ rate).
- `fig_conversion_chain.png`: Indices population -> households -> dwellings -> floor area -> carbon; intensity per m².
- `mc_3_sobol.png`: Sobol indices (reference): within-scenario parametric uncertainty only.
- `sens_2_paths.png`: Annual paths of the largest one-at-a-time sensitivities.
- `boss_06_cumulative_carbon_pb.png`: PB variant of boss_06: cumulative carbon vs cumulative AR and AtP boundaries.
- `pb_5_demand_vs_boundary.png`: Annual carbon by demand type (in scope, S3-10) against the AR and AtP boundaries.
